nodes.title: Revenue recognition
nodes.focus: Revenue is recognised when the applicable recognition criteria are met, which can differ from cash collection.
nodes.hook: Which accounts change when this transaction happens?

nodes.title: Trade receivables
nodes.focus: Amounts owed by customers for recognised sales; collection converts the receivable into cash.
nodes.hook: Where did this balance come from, and what transaction would change it?

nodes.title: Inventory
nodes.focus: Goods held for sale or used in production, measured under the applicable accounting framework.
nodes.hook: Where did this balance come from, and what transaction would change it?

nodes.title: Trade payables
nodes.focus: Amounts owed to suppliers for goods or services already received.
nodes.hook: Where did this balance come from, and what transaction would change it?

nodes.title: Operating working capital
nodes.focus: Operating current assets less operating current liabilities, using an explicit definition that usually excludes cash and financing debt.
nodes.hook: Can a growing business run out of cash before customers pay?

nodes.title: Operating cash flow
nodes.focus: Cash generated or used by operating activities, classified under the applicable reporting framework.
nodes.hook: Why might cash move differently from reported profit?

nodes.title: Capital expenditure
nodes.focus: Cash invested in qualifying long-lived operating assets; it is distinct from the period depreciation expense.
nodes.hook: Why might cash move differently from reported profit?

nodes.title: Depreciation
nodes.focus: Allocation of a depreciable asset cost over its useful life; generally a non-cash expense in the period.
nodes.hook: Can this change reported profit without changing cash today?

nodes.title: EBIT
nodes.focus: Earnings before interest and tax; specify adjustments and reconcile it with reported operating profit.
nodes.hook: Can this change reported profit without changing cash today?

nodes.title: NOPAT
nodes.focus: After-tax operating profit for the specified operating perimeter; a simplified model uses EBIT multiplied by one minus an operating tax rate.
nodes.hook: Does this valuation use the right cash flow for the right investor?

nodes.title: Free cash flow to the firm (FCFF)
nodes.focus: Cash available to all capital providers after operating taxes and reinvestment, before financing distributions.
nodes.hook: Does this valuation use the right cash flow for the right investor?

nodes.title: Free cash flow to equity (FCFE)
nodes.focus: Cash available to equity after reinvestment, debt cash flows and other relevant financing claims.
nodes.hook: Does this valuation use the right cash flow for the right investor?

nodes.title: Weighted average cost of capital (WACC)
nodes.focus: Market-value-weighted required return on the financing mix, with applicable debt tax treatment.
nodes.hook: Which investor claim bears this risk and which return compensates for it?

nodes.title: Cost of equity
nodes.focus: Required return of equity investors for the risk of the equity claim.
nodes.hook: Which investor claim bears this risk and which return compensates for it?

nodes.title: Enterprise value
nodes.focus: Value of the specified operating enterprise available to its capital providers; reconcile the perimeter to equity value.
nodes.hook: Does this valuation use the right cash flow for the right investor?

nodes.title: Equity value
nodes.focus: Value attributable to common equity after the relevant non-equity claims and non-operating adjustments.
nodes.hook: Does this valuation use the right cash flow for the right investor?

nodes.title: Expected credit losses
nodes.focus: Probability-weighted credit-loss estimates under the applicable impairment framework.
nodes.hook: Could this borrower repay under a plausible downside scenario?

nodes.title: Net borrowing
nodes.focus: Cash proceeds from new debt less cash principal repayments over the specified period.
nodes.hook: Why might cash move differently from reported profit?

nodes.title: Discounted cash flow (DCF)
nodes.focus: Value expected future cash flows by discounting at a rate matched to their risk, currency and investor claim.
nodes.hook: Does this valuation use the right cash flow for the right investor?

nodes.title: Return on invested capital (ROIC)
nodes.focus: After-tax operating profit relative to the invested capital used to generate it, using consistent timing and scope.
nodes.hook: Could this ratio improve while the underlying business becomes weaker?

edges.why: Double entry lets one transaction be traced through accounts and statements.

edges.conditions: Hold other cash-flow components fixed and apply the reporting framework.

edges.why: Credit-loss expense can reduce reported profit without a contemporaneous cash payment.
Depreciation reduces EBIT for depreciating operating assets.

edges.why: Cash operating capital expenditure is deducted when calculating standard FCFF.
edges.conditions: Keep acquisitions and non-operating investments explicitly classified.

edges.conditions: Adjust separately for excluded non-operating assets and claims.

edges.why: The enterprise-to-equity bridge reconciles operating value to shareholder value.
